sourcedFrom: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) (UNDATED — Beretta prints a form code rather than a year in these books)
cleanIntro: A tip-up barrel changes the whole job: there is no need to rack a slide to check the chamber, and no need to run a rod down from the muzzle. Press the barrel latch, the barrel swings up, and you can see and reach the chamber directly. Beretta asks for cleaning every time the pistol is fired, or at least once a year.

steps.title: Barrel latch first — the chamber is right there
steps.action: Press the barrel latch and the barrel tips up, exposing the chamber. Take out any chambered cartridge, then drop the magazine. On a tip-up the chamber check is the easiest one in the pistol world; there is no excuse for skipping it.
steps.aside: lt is advisable to carry out the field stripping and the assembly operations over a table to catch components, should they drop.
steps.quote: Press the barrel latch to release the barrel. Remove the chambered cartridge.
steps.cite: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) — UNLOADING THE PISTOL AND MAGAZINE, printed p.18

steps.title: Safety OFF and the hammer fully cocked
steps.action: The strip is done with the hammer COCKED and the safety disengaged — the opposite of most pistols, and the reason a Tomcat sometimes refuses to come apart for someone doing it by habit. Prove the chamber empty first, then cock it.
steps.aside: MAKE SURE THE PISTOL IS UNLOADED. IF NOT, UNLOAD
steps.cite: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY — Field Stripping, printed p.19-20

steps.title: Barrel forward over its hinge to a solid stop
steps.action: Swing the barrel forward over its hinge until it reaches a SOLID stop — past the normal loading position. That extra travel is what clears the hinge for the slide to come off.
steps.quote: Swing the barrel forward over its hinge until it reaches a solid stop.
steps.cite: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY — Field Stripping, printed p.19-20

steps.title: ⛔ Slide back about 1/8 inch, lift the front, listen for the click
steps.action: Retract the slide only about an eighth of an inch and lift its FRONT up over the barrel hinge. A sharp click tells you the recoil spring has disengaged from the slide. Wait for that click — pulling the slide further back without it is fighting the spring, not releasing it.
steps.aside: A sharp click indicates the disengagement of the recoil spring from the slide.
steps.quote: Retract the slide about 1/8 inch and lift the front of the slide over the barrel hinge.
steps.cite: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY — Field Stripping, printed p.19-20

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame — strip complete
steps.action: Once the click has happened, pull the slide forward until it clears the frame guide lugs. Frame, slide, barrel: that is the whole published strip. Beretta recommends anything further be a gunsmith's job.
steps.aside: Beretta recommends any further disassembly be performed by a qualified gunsmith.
steps.quote: Once the sharp click is heard, pull the slide forward until it clears the frame guide lugs.
steps.cite: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) — DISASSEMBLY — Field Stripping, printed p.19-20

steps.title: Barrel from the chamber end, then the lug and locking surface
steps.action: Bore solvent and a brush, always starting at the CHAMBER end, then dry patches, repeating until it is clean. Then wipe the outside of the barrel and lug assembly with a solvent patch, let it dry, and lubricate the lug and locking surface before a light oil inside and out.
steps.aside: Lightly oil the inside and outside of the barrel, using a clean patch soaked in gun oil.
steps.quote: Clean the barrel with bore solvent and a brush and then dry it with cleaning patches. Always begin at the chamber end. Repeat until the barrel is clean.
steps.cite: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE — Barrel, printed p.21

steps.title: Slide: breech face, extractor, rails, underside of the breech
steps.action: Cloth or brush with gun oil over the slide, and give the breech face, the extractor, the rails and the underside of the breech particular attention. Wipe it clean, oil it lightly, and put a few drops down the rails.
steps.aside: Lightly oil the slide. Apply a few drops of oil down the rails of the slide.
steps.quote: Clean the slide with a cloth and/or brush soaked in gun oil, paying special attention to the breech face, extractor, slide rails and under side of breech.
steps.cite: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE — Slide, printed p.21

steps.title: Frame, then the magazine — and rotate carry ammunition
steps.action: Oil-soaked rag or brush over every area carrying powder residue, then wipe clean and lightly lubricate the rails and moving parts — magazine catch, trigger system, hammer and sear by name. Clean the magazines and wipe them with a lightly oiled rag. If this pistol is carried loaded, unload the magazines periodically and inspect the cartridges.
steps.aside: If the pistol is carried with chamber and magazine loaded, it is important to periodically unload all magazines for cartridge inspection.
steps.quote: Wipe clean and lightly lubricate rails and moving parts. Be sure to oil the, magazine catch, trigger system, hammer, and sear
steps.cite: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) — MAINTENANCE — Frame / Magazine, printed p.21

steps.title: Grips come off only if it is genuinely filthy — 10 lb·in going back
steps.action: Beretta's position on the grip panels is that removal is only necessary if the pistol is excessively dirty, so leave them on for a routine clean. If they do come off, flat-head screwdriver counter-clockwise, and going back they are torqued to 10 lb·in — snug, not gorilla-tight, because the frame under them is not steel.
steps.aside: Tighten the grip screws to a torque of 10 lb·in.
steps.quote: Note: The grip removal is only necessary if the pistol is excessively dirty.
steps.cite: Beretta Tomcat & Bobcat User Manual — UQAN4110 rev 3 (form code printed in the running header) — Grip Panels Remove and Install, printed p.20

deepAbsentReason: Beretta stops the owner at the field strip on the tip-up pistols and prints it twice: "Beretta recommends any further disassembly be performed by a qualified gunsmith" at the end of the strip, and "The firearm should not be disassembled for cleaning beyond what is described" in maintenance. The grip-panel removal is published and is carried as a cleaning step, but it is not a deeper strip — and a manufacturer's published DON'T outranks every other tier, so nothing deeper is authored from anywhere else.

cleaning.name: BARREL
tasks: Solvent and brush from the CHAMBER end, always
Dry patches until one comes out clean
Lug and locking surface wiped, dried, then lubricated
Light oil inside and outside before it goes back

cleaning.name: SLIDE
tasks: Breech face, extractor, rails and the underside of the breech
Wipe clean, light oil, a few drops down the rails

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Powder residue off every surface it has reached
Light lube on the rails, magazine catch, trigger system, hammer and sear

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE & CARRY AMMUNITION
tasks: Magazines cleaned, then wiped with a lightly oiled rag
⛔ Never spray or apply oil to cartridges
If carried loaded, unload the magazines periodically and inspect the rounds

reassembly: Grips back on first if they came off, screws to 10 lb·in.
Elevate the front of the slide and place its rear over the frame just in front of the frame's guide lugs.
Pull the slide rails back over the guide lugs while lowering the front of the slide to rest gently on the recoil spring levers.
⛔ Press down on the FRONT of the slide until it CLICKS — that click is the recoil spring engaging the slide cutouts, and without it the pistol is not assembled.
Check by eye that the underside of the slide sits flat on the frame's sliding surface — slide and frame parallel.
Swing the barrel down into the closed position and verify the barrel lever closes.
Retract and release the slide to check function, lower the hammer, engage the safety.
fncheck: Reassembled and unloaded: verify the safety is engaged, insert an EMPTY magazine and retract the slide so it stays open, then pull it back and release it to close. Swing the barrel down and check the barrel lever closes properly. Retract and release the slide once more to check function, lower the hammer under thumb control, and engage the safety — red dot not showing.
